run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T00:59:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy coincides with a ~12-minute burst of frontend-proxy ingress error spans (ratio 0.0006 baseline -> 0.0802 peak at 01:08, error-span rate ~1.04/s). The traces show two failure shapes: HTTP 504 after exactly ~15.0s (frontend /api/data 19.7-22.2s, driven by frontend's grpc GetAds call to ad 11-21s, which in turn waited 1.4-4.4s on flagd ResolveBoolean calls that ended in grpc status 4), and HTTP 500 from frontend with grpc status 14 'UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (100.70.197.56 is the ClusterIP of Service ad). The ad Deployment's pod was replaced by a rollout restart at 01:00:27-01:00:29 (ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:00:27Z); the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh then burned CPU at its 50m limit (0.032-0.049 cores/s) and was CFS-throttled 0.95-0.99 of periods through ~01:11, decaying to 0.26-0.30 by 01:14-01:18, exactly matching the window in which frontend GetAds errors went from zero to 1.01/s and back to zero. flagd was checked and was not throttled (0) and served ResolveBoolean in microseconds, so the multi-second flag delays sit on the ad client side. Thus the fault originates in the ad Deployment (otel-demo): a fresh ad pod under a 50m CPU limit was throttled ~99% and could not answer frontend within Envoy's 15s timeout, which is what frontend-proxy recorded as request errors. Baseline frontend-proxy errors (<=0.0012, e.g. 503s at 00:54-00:57) predate the deviation and are background; frontend-proxy's own CPU throttling (0.279 at 01:08 vs 0.289 at 00:55) did not change, so the proxy is the victim, not the source. An ad pod restart is a mechanism; its trigger (who issued the rollout restart at 01:00:27) is not visible because change history is not integrated, and the flagd-config fault flag adFailure=on does not match the observed failure path (ad returned grpc status 0; failures were timeouts and connection refusals).

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own ingress error spans deviated sharply inside the window: the per-minute 5m error-span rate was 0 until 01:01:07, rose from 0.211/s at 01:02:07 to a peak of 1.037/s at 01:08:07, and fell back to ~0.015/s by 01:14:07-01:18:07, while the surrounding requests stayed roughly constant (~12-12.7 spans/s of STATUS_CODE_UNSET on ingress).
The frontend-proxy ingress error ratio (error spans / all ingress spans) was 0.00029-0.00117 before the deviation, peaked at 0.08019 at 01:08:07 and was back to 0.00148-0.00438 by 01:14:07-01:18:07.

frontend-proxy's error spans in the burst are HTTP 504 with durations of exactly ~15,000,000 us (e.g. ingress span f0923dbb3431a584: duration_us 15000154, http.status_code 504, error=true) plus HTTP 500 and 503 responses; over the 84-minute window the ingress span count was 24393.5 UNSET vs 427.2 ERROR.

Traces at 01:07:48-01:07:49 show the 504 path end to end: frontend GET /api/data spans of 19.7-22.2s with HTTP 200/500 inside, frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds of 15.19-21.36s, ad server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds of 15.20-20.97s (rpc.grpc.status_code 0), and ad client spans flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean of 2.10-4.40s with error=true and rpc.grpc.status_code 4.

ad server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds durations of 5.30s, 7.20s and 9.03s were captured at 01:08:02-01:08:14 together with ad client ResolveBoolean spans of 1.47-2.50s (two marked rpc.grpc.status_code 4), while flagd's own span for the same call completed in 79 us.

A second failure shape at 01:07:40 is an immediate failure: frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed in 299-381 us with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and grpc.error_message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080 (2025-12-15T17:53:00.348Z)", producing frontend HTTP 500 and frontend-proxy ingress HTTP 500 spans; 100.70.197.56:8080 is the ClusterIP/port of Service ad in namespace otel-demo.

frontend's own GetAds error rate was 0 from 00:39:07 through 01:01:07, then rose (0.181/s at 01:02:07, 0.993/s at 01:08:07, peak 1.015/s) and returned to 0 from 01:14:07 onward; over the same period frontend's error spans are concentrated on operations GET /api/data (393.46), executing api route (pages) /api/data (393.46) and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (393.62).

Deployment ad in namespace otel-demo was rolled out at 01:00:27-01:00:29: event 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' at 01:00:27Z, ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 'Created pod: ad-785b4464f5-9bshh' at 01:00:27Z, 'Stopping container ad' on pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' at 01:00:29Z; the new pod reports startTime 2026-11-17T01:00:27Z.

The pod-template change that produced ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 is a restart marker, not a configuration change: ad-785b4464f5's pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:00:27Z, and both ad-554b849958 (revision 1) and ad-785b4464f5 (revision 2) have identical container specs - image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, env FLAGD_HOST=flagd FLAGD_PORT=8013, resources limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The replacement ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was almost continuously CPU-throttled: CFS throttled-periods ratio 0.9497-0.9709 at 01:00:07-01:02:07, 0.9867 at 01:04:07, 0.9942 at 01:06:07, 0.9487 at 01:10:07, then 0.6719 at 01:12:07 and 0.2593-0.2997 at 01:14:07-01:18:07, versus 0.0823-0.2901 for the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc.

The new ad pod's CPU usage ran at its 50m ceiling during the burst: 0.0318 cores/s at 01:04:07, 0.0489 at 01:06:07, 0.0494 at 01:08:07 and 0.0454 at 01:10:07, versus 0.0015-0.0085 cores/s for the previous ad pod.

Among all otel-demo pods, the ad pod was the clear throttling outlier at 01:08:00 (ad-785b4464f5-9bshh 0.9888; next highest cart-755465879b-htjh5 0.5192, fraud-detection 0.3575, frontend 0.2787), whereas at 00:55:00 the top throttled pod was frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw at 0.2894 and the then-current ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was at 0.1530.

Service ad has no readiness, liveness or startup probe on its container, so the container had no probe-based defence or startup grace that could have kept a CPU-starved pod out of the Service endpoints before it could answer.
flagd was not resource-starved during the window: the flagd container of pod flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr had a CFS throttled-periods ratio of exactly 0 at every 2-minute step from 00:39:07 to 01:18:07.

flagd's own ResolveBoolean spans are microsecond-scale during the incident - successful ones at 79 us, 67 us, 66 us, 49 us, 44 us and 4-5 us, and the error spans carry otel.status_description "context deadline exceeded" with durations of only 25 us and 59 us - so the multi-second delays observed on ad's client spans were not spent inside flagd's handler.

Before the alert's deviation the frontend-proxy service already produced a low background error ratio (<=0.0012); sampled background spans from 00:54:31-00:57:45 are ingress HTTP 503 responses of 26-534 ms to load-generator user_index/user_browse_product with no frontend spans in the trace at all.
The current flagd configuration ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo) declares flag adFailure with defaultVariant "on" ("Fail ad service"), while adHighCpu and adManualGc are defaultVariant "off".

fraud-detection is a separate change during the window: its container reports lastState terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-17T00:35:05Z and restartCount 1, and events record 'Created container: fraud-detection' / 'Started container: fraud-detection' on pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 at 01:07:17-01:07:18Z; all 21 otel-demo pods, including ad-785b4464f5-9bshh and flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr, were Running and ready at query time.

frontend-proxy's own resource pressure did not deviate at the time of its errors: its pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw had a CFS throttled-periods ratio of 0.2787 at 01:08:00 versus 0.2894 at 00:55:00, and its 504 spans last exactly the ~15s Envoy route timeout while the upstream frontend spans in the same traces last 19.7-22.2s, so the proxy was waiting on its upstream rather than being the degraded component.

The error burst is explained by CPU starvation of the replacement ad pod: the new ad container demanded far more CPU than its 50m limit allowed (usage pinned at 0.045-0.049 cores/s with 0.95-0.99 CFS throttling), so its gRPC handling stretched to 5-21s per GetAds and its flagd ResolveBoolean calls to 1.4-4.4s (client-side deadline exceeded against a microsecond-fast flagd), which pushed frontend /api/data past frontend-proxy's 15s route timeout (504) and sometimes left frontend's channel with no usable connection (500/UNAVAILABLE). The decay of throttling to 0.26-0.30 by 01:14 matches the error rate returning to baseline at the same time.

The immediate 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' failures reflect the ad Service having no accepting backend during the pod replacement / its CPU-starved state (either a brief endpoint gap around the 01:00:29 pod kill or a listener that could not accept under throttling); the evidence shows the client-side error and its target Service but not which of these two mechanisms applied at that instant.

flagd as the cause of the latency: rejected - the flagd container was never CFS-throttled (ratio 0 for the whole window) and its ResolveBoolean spans were served in 4-112 us, including successful evaluations of the same calls that ad's client spans show taking seconds; the slow segment is between ad's client and flagd, on the ad side.

The enabled fault-injection flag adFailure in flagd-config as the cause of this error burst: rejected - the declared fault is 'Fail ad service', but the observed ad GetAds spans completed with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (no failure status) and the frontend-side failures were 14 UNAVAILABLE / 15s timeouts, not an error reported by ad; the observed path is latency and connection refusal, not an ad-reported failure.

The fraud-detection container OOMKill/restart as the cause of the frontend-proxy error rate: rejected - the OOMKill is recorded at 00:35:05Z, before the error deviation, and the failing traces examined run frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ad -> flagd without a fraud-detection span; no evidence ties that restart to frontend-proxy's error spans.

Give the ad container realistic CPU headroom (the 50m limit is the shortfall that produced 95-99% CFS throttling on the fresh pod) and add a startup/readiness probe with enough initial delay so a warming pod is not serving; then verify the CFS throttled-periods ratio for the ad pod returns to its pre-incident ~0.08-0.15 range.

Trace who issued the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T01:00:27Z (the restartedAt annotation is the only change marker; change history is not integrated in this investigation) and schedule such restarts with surge/PDB so the ad Service always keeps a serving endpoint.

Because frontend-proxy already carried a nonzero background error ratio (<=0.0012, e.g. 503s at 00:54-00:57) while the alert fires on rate above 0, the RequestErrorRate threshold should be reviewed to require a sustained ratio well above that background, and the baseline 503-with-no-frontend-span errors should be investigated separately.

Confirm whether the flagd-config flag adFailure with defaultVariant "on" is intended in this environment; it declares a fault ('Fail ad service') that did not manifest in the observed traces, so either the flag is not consumed as expected or it should be turned off to avoid an unexplained armed fault.

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T01:00:27Z (the restartedAt annotation) cannot be verified.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rows, so its exact expression, threshold and evaluation basis are unknown; the annotation's 'current: 2.4555' cannot be mapped to the span-metric ratios observed here (peak 0.0802 = 8.0%).

The alert start time 2026-11-17T00:59:07Z precedes the visible error deviation (first elevated 5m error rate at 01:02:07, seen also as frontend GetAds errors starting 01:02:07); whether the alert fired earlier on the small background error ratio (<=0.0012, present from 00:44) or on a different measurement could not be determined.

A query for GetAds spans slower than 5s in 2026-11-16T23:59:07Z-01:00:00Z (operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, service ad) returned no traces, but that is an empty query result, not proof of absence of slow requests before 01:00.

The previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was deleted, so its container logs are unavailable; the new pod's retained logs start at 01:10:37, so the 01:00:27-01:10:37 startup interval (JVM warm-up, GC, OTel export behaviour) is unobserved.

Historical endpoint/ready-replica state for Service/Deployment ad is not observable: queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available series returned nothing, so it cannot be decided whether the ECONNREFUSED came from an empty endpoint set during the rollout or from a starved listener on the new pod.

Historical flagd flag values are not observable (only the current ConfigMap content was read), so whether adHighCpu or adManualGc were ever enabled during 01:00-01:13 - which would also explain heavy CPU work in the ad JVM - cannot be confirmed or excluded from configuration history.
Whether the frontend-proxy error ratio returned fully to baseline after the window is unknown: the last usable sample is 0.004379 at 01:18:07, above the 0.0006-0.0012 pre-incident values.

No metrics exist for service flagd in traces_span_metrics (flagd is absent from the traces_span_metrics_calls_total service_name list), so flagd's own error and latency trends had to be judged only from sampled Jaeger spans and container CPU throttling.
next_steps: Raise the ad container CPU request/limit (or remove the 50m cap) and re-check container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total for the ad pod after the change; add a startup/readiness probe aligned with application warm-up.

Review the change record for the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T01:00:27Z once a change-history source is available, and add a PodDisruptionBudget/surge policy so restarts keep a serving ad endpoint.
Confirm the intent of flagd-config demo.flagd.json: adFailure is currently armed (defaultVariant "on") but produced no observable ad failures; adHighCpu and adManualGc are off.

Re-baseline the RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy so that the small background error ratio (<=0.0012) does not fire it, and separately investigate the background Envoy 503s that show no frontend spans.
If the ad readiness mechanism matters, add a probe and monitor kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready for ad so that future endpoint gaps are measurable rather than inferred.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
